title: ST-depression–chronotropic interactions did not establish incremental diagnostic value across Cleveland and Hungarian cohorts
abstract: We tested four interactions between exercise ST depression and age-normalized peak heart rate against conventional noninvasive predictors with flexible additive terms. Logistic models trained on303 Cleveland patients were frozen and evaluated on293 Hungarian patients from a separately named clinical cohort. Target Brier error decreased from0.130995 to0.126343, but the joint source-refit/target-bootstrap95% interval for the difference was[-0.034404,0.023021]. A simpler linear baseline performed better than either primary model, and complete-case performance reversed the apparent advantage. Incremental diagnostic improvement was not established. These summary-field interactions do not implement the established ST/HR index, and historical selected angiography cohorts cannot establish clinical utility.
